title: How a C# program works — interview

items.question: How is C# different from TypeScript at run time?
items.answer: C# is compiled to IL with CTS metadata; the CLR enforces types. TypeScript is a compile-time checker that emits JavaScript; the engine never sees those types. Node and the CLR are different hosts even if both handle an SQS JSON body.
followUps: Where does the Common Type System sit relative to the C# language?
What does `dotnet build` produce that `tsc` does not?
items.sixtySeconds: C# keeps types in the assembly; TS erases them. CLR versus V8. Same AWS event, different process.

items.question: Walk source to CPU for a typical worker.
items.answer: Roslyn emits IL into a DLL. The CLR JIT compiles methods (tiered). Optionally Native AOT compiles ahead of time for a native binary. That is not `node file.js`.
followUps: Is an assembly the same as an ES module?
items.sixtySeconds: Source → IL assembly → JIT, or AOT to native. Assembly is a metadata unit, not an import graph.

items.question: How do you choose the C# language version?
items.answer: It follows the target framework. net10.0 means C# 14. Override LangVersion only when you must; never latest, because it tracks the installed compiler.
followUps: How do you print the compiler’s chosen version?
items.sixtySeconds: TFM selects LangVersion. Pin TFM, not latest. Implicit usings are generated global usings.

items.question: What is the entry point of a new console app?
items.answer: Top-level statements in one file; the compiler synthesizes Main. Classic static Main is equivalent. Two top-level files fail to compile. args is string[].
followUps: Can file-based apps use Main instead of top-level statements?
What happens if you await at the top level?
items.sixtySeconds: One entry: top-level or Main. Compiler synthesizes the rest. args is the argv vector.

items.question: What is a file-based app in .NET 10?
items.answer: A single .cs file run with the SDK, no csproj. C# 14 #: directives set packages, properties, SDK. Convert with dotnet project convert when it grows.
items.sixtySeconds: C# 14 / .NET 10: dotnet run file.cs, #: directives, optional convert to project.
